text:
rachel: Filing this here since it tripped up a customer in the Go quickstart. When a long stream is resumed after auth refresh we sometimes see two logical SSE events merged into one because the resumed chunk doesn't begin with a blank line separator. Repro in the Go SDK sample app with default timeouts.

tom: do you have the raw fragments? i'm guessing the resume chunk lost the leading "\n\n" boundary so the client appended and the parser treated it as one data block.

rachel: paste from the proxy capture:
```
--- initial connection ---
chunk A: "id: 77\nevent: delta\ndata: first part of message"
chunk B: " data continued\n\n"
--- client times out & refreshes token ---
--- reconnect with Last-Event-ID: 77 ---
chunk C (resume): "id: 78\nevent: delta\ndata:second message no-leading-space\n\n"
```
If the client was holding a partial line ending with `\n` (no double newline), the naive concatenation becomes:
`first part of message data continueddata:second message no-leading-space`
which surfaces as a garbled single message to the app.

vishal: this is subtly different than simple duplicate-id problems. Here the resumed chunk lacks the expected boundary so the parser's split-on-"\n\n" logic doesn't separate events. JS SDK amortizes this because we trim/normalize leading newlines on reconnect + dedupe ids; Go SDK's parser keeps a running `partialLine` buffer and only emits on blank-line delimiters.

grace: two practical mitigations: 1) make quickstart default `stream_timeout` longer (customers hitting small timeouts cause frequent resumes), 2) on resume, client should drop any leading newline-free partial buffer before concatenating, and always scan incoming data for an `id:` line and ignore frames with id <= Last-Event-ID.

tom: additional thought: the server side should guarantee event boundaries on resume. If server resumes in the middle of an event, it should retransmit the remainder prefixed by `\n\n` or repeat the whole event. But we can't rely on all proxies doing that, so client hardening is required.

rachel: added a small reproducer in `examples/go/stream-resume-repro` that simulates a proxy chopping the gap. I'll attach logs to the GH issue.

vishal: proposed client changes for Go SDK: 
- on reconnect with Last-Event-ID, flush partial buffer (drop incomplete trailing data)
- treat any incoming `id:` header as an atomic marker and dedupe by id before emitting
- normalize incoming bytes: replace `\r\n` and `\r` with `\n`, then split on `\n\n` but also accept `\nid:` as a boundary (defensive)

grace: let's also add a small integration test that runs with extreme timing: token refresh latency + artificial chunk-splitting so we don't regress. I can add that to the flaky suite.

ci-bot: ci: build #2026.04.02-214 failed 1 tests flaky: sdk_go_stream_resume_test.go. https://ci.redwood.example/2026/214

tom: for the short term, docs patch: call out `stream_timeout` default in quickstart and add a note in SDK parity doc that Go currently needs the patch to match JS dedupe behavior. rachel can we include the reproducer link in that doc?

rachel: yes, will open PR with reproducer, small sdk patch (flush partial on resume + id filter), and doc note. tagging @grace for the integration test.

vishal: after the PR: stress-run with 50 parallel clients, random auth delays, and proxy chunk-splits. If green, we can backport to the last minor.

grace: also let's update sample-app to set `stream_timeout: 90s` instead of 15s so new users don't hit this by default.

rachel: thanks all. i'll ping the channel when PR lands. :rocket:
